utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. May I remind you of the affirmation which you took at the beginning of your evidence that still applies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to all in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Susic. Since we speak the same language, could you please pause before answering my questions, so that the interpreters would interpret everything you say; like you gave your answers to Mr. Bulatovic, so that we'd have everything in the transcript. Mr. Susic, until now, before courts, the special court in Belgrade, before investigation agencies, you did not give any evidence with regard to what you are testifying about here?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right. I have made no such statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: So you were not even asked to testify before the military court in 1998 in the proceedings against any perpetrators of the war crime at the Ovcara crime?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: They cannot hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: The security organisation of the Guards Brigade and the military investigation agencies, in the period from until 2001, did they know where you were, or rather, up until the 20th of November, 1991, and what duties you were involved in at that time in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could Mr. Vasic please turn off his microphone when the witness is speaking.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And they knew when we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that in the proceedings before the military court and in other proceedings, the generals Milorad Panic, General Lukic, Colonel Vukasinovic were asked to testify, and they made statements in such proceedings?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we're going to move on to a different subject. Yesterday, you described how you came to the area of Vukovar and what the tasks of your unit were. You mentioned that the anti-terrorist company and the 2nd Company of military police of the 1st Battalion, almost immediately upon their arrival, were attached to the 2nd Assault Detachment that was commanded by then Lieutenant-Colonel Lukic; is that right? Did I understand that right.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But at that time, he was Major Lukic, and the 2nd anti-terrorist detachment was attached on the 2nd of October; whereas, the 2nd Company of the APCs was attached on the 4th.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Just a correction in the transcript in line 25 on page 2, the witness said that the anti-terrorist company was on the 2nd of October attached; whereas, the 2nd company of the APCs was attached on the 4th. Yes. Thank you. Tell me, these two attached companies remained within the 2nd Assault Detachment until what date?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The anti-terrorist company up until the 20th of October; whereas, the 2nd Company until the end of the activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: What is the "end" mean, does that mean the 24th of November?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the 24th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The 1st Battalion of the military police, towards the end of October, 1991, excluding these two units that were attached to other units, was it within another assault detachment?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not until then. But on the 1st, a unit was established that took part in combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: When you say the 1st, do you mean --

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 1st of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Tell me, was that the 5th Assault Detachment and, if so, who commanded that unit?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was the 5th Assault Detachment and then the anti-terrorist company was within it, and also parts of the military police company that I commanded.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Am I right if I conclude that you commanded that unit in the actions that took place on the 14th, 15th, 16th and 17th of November in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: As for this time that you are -- or rather, that I am referring to from the 14th of November onwards, who commanded the units that were attached from your unit to the 2nd Assault Detachment?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, there was only the 2nd Company within the assault detachment, and it was commanded by Major Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember about the period between the 14th and the 17th of November, did you receive any tasks from the brigade command; and if you remember, briefly, what kind of tasks were they, that is to say, you as the 1st Battalion of the military police?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These tasks were aimed at securing convoys and combat activities that took place on the axis of activity of the 1st and 2nd Assault Detachments.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: In this period, did you have some contacts with the 4th Assault Detachment? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have any such contact.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, when you received these orders that we are talking about now, how did you receive them, in which way? These orders to attack on the 14th, 16th, 17th?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The orders were issued in writing; and later on, things were added in case there were some corrections at the briefings themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As commander of the 1st Battalion of the military police, did you have radio communication with the brigade command, or rather, of the Operations Group South in Negoslavci?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I always had communication with my command.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Just explain what kind of communication that was, and who was it specifically that you communicated with at the command in Negoslavci?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had communications equipment that, according to establishment, belonged to my unit; that was wire communication, jaguar, then I had communications with the operation centre and directly with the commander, when necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did you communicate with the commander through the operation centre or directly?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when I wanted to speak to the commander himself, then he was the one who would speak to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. During combat activities in Vukovar, did you get any orders from Miodrag Panic, Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: And the chief of the security organ or Vukasinovic, his deputy?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who had the task of securing the command post in Negoslavci, which unit?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Negoslavci, the command post was secured by the 1st Company of APCs, parts of the military police company, and the traffic company, minus one platoon, which provided traffic security to the logistics command post in Berak.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Are all of these units that belong to the 1st Battalion of the military police, whose commander you became at one point in time?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those are the units involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Who was responsible for providing security of the command post in Negoslavci? I'm now referring to the actual officers involved. Who was responsible for securing this command post in accordance with regulations?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up until the 1st of November, it was Major Kavalic. After the 1st of November, it was I. Captain Bozic was on the line, and he was exercising control as to how this was taking place.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you know that at one point in time, a command of Negoslavci was established; and, if so, who was the commander?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm aware of this command, that it was established, and it was Major Vukasinovic who was its commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: After the town command was established, did Major Vukasinovic issue any commands to organs of the military police who were securing the command in Negoslavci and also the exit/entry checkpoints in Negoslavci?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was not in charge of commanding personnel; he was issuing these passes and saying what was to be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Are you saying that as town commander, he did not command the units that were securing that particular locality?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was not commanding them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Can you explain what the function of the town commander is? What are his powers, if you know, of course?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not town commander of that town, so I don't know. But he was supposed to regulate everything; and if he needed personnel, then he had to ask for such personnel to be approved. If a desk was supposed to be set up somewhere, he would issue the order and we would actually carry this through.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Since you do not have information about what the actual powers are, I'm not going to ask you anything else about the powers of the town commander. But tell me, can a commander of a unit transfer some of his powers to another officer from that unit in terms of carrying out a particular task?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He can, but he still remains responsible for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Can this authority be transferred to the security organ of that unit?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know about that because I was never in such a situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: What about Major Vukasinovic, was he in that sort of situation in as far as you know, since he is a security officer was, after all, appointed a town commander in Negoslavci; am I right?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was appointed commander; that's a fact. And he was responsible for the entire security of the command post. But when he needed men to carry out an assignment, he would address us and we provided those.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday, in answer to my learned friend Bulatovic's question, you talked about the daily briefings that took place in Negoslavci at 1800 hours. If you look at all the regular combat reports sent by the command of OG South, it appears that they are in relation to the time period between 1800 hours on one day and 1800 hours on the next day, which means they cover a 24-hour period, which means that these meetings were supposed to be held before 1800 hours every day, so that by 1800 hours, a report could be submitted. Would I be right, based on your recollection, or not?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know whether you're right or not, but briefings were held at about 1800 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You implied to Mr. Bulatovic yesterday that you remember the briefing that was held on the 19th of November, 1991. No mention was made of the hospital evacuation, of that briefing. Is that a fair assessment of your testimony on Friday?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's a fair assessment. At any briefing, I would just write down my own assignments or anything that was said that concerned me. Most tasks received in a situation of combat are difficult ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Is it possible, then, that the hospital evacuation was discussed on that day, but the simple fact was you didn't write it down because you had no role to play in this evacuation or no specific role to play?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a fair statement. I never received an assignment like that, and I do not know that this was discussed at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if, on the 18th of November, anything was said at that briefing about the surrender of the Croatian forces?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 18th of November, they had surrendered already by the time we got to the briefing at 1800 hours. The surrender had already been completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Was that on the agenda of that particular briefing?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on the agenda. The Mitnica Battalion had surrendered and had been disarmed. There were a lot of civilians who took refuge in the Velepromet holding centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Was any reference made to Ovcara at that briefing?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The reason being, the Mitnica Battalion were put up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if any other important subjects were raised at that particular meeting? Would you please share that with us?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I could comment on anything in particular.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: But what if I told you that an international delegation was to arrive on the 19th, does that jog your memory? Was there anything you had to do concerning that delegation? Do you remember anything like that being planned for the 19th of November at all?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Are you aware at all of the fact a Cyrus Vance arrived in Vukovar on the 19th of November?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did you receive any sort of assignment concerning his visit?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was there to set up security, and this was indeed carried out by the 1st Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: You received this assignment on the evening of the 18th at the briefing; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember specifically when I received it, but I know that I did and I know that I carried it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you remember preparing your unit for securing Cyrus Vance; what day, what time?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that, in particular. There were lots of preparations being carried out so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Who secured Cyrus Vance during his visit to the Vukovar barracks on the 19th of November? Is this something you remember?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the time he entered this area until the time he left, he was being secured by the 1st Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember any briefing at all where the hospital evacuation was discussed and assignments were handed out?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: What if I told you that we heard evidence here by witnesses who claimed that on the 19th of November, the hospital evacuation was, in fact, discussed and that Major Sljivancanin was put in charge of that task; would that jog your memory?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wouldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: You've answered. But all the same, let me re-ask this question: Did any of the units of your 1st Battalion take part in anything to do with the hospital evacuation?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Was any unit from the 1st Battalion of the military police involved in escorting the convoy of civilians from Velepromet on the 19th of November?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Can you specify which unit?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1st Company and the Traffic Company. On the 19th, they both escorted the POWs from Ovcara to Sremska Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: On the 19th, they escorted the prisoners from Mitnica as far as Sremska Mitrovica?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those who were originally from Mitnica were escorted as far as Sremska Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: But they escorted a convoy from Velepromet, too; the one that left for Sremska Mitrovica, am I right?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a convoy headed for the border. I'm not sure if that was the one, but I am sure that they escorted the civilians from Velepromet, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know if members of the 2nd Military Police Battalion were involved in the hospital evacuation in any way at all?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know they secured the hospital itself. And I know that every time a bus arrived there, there would be two military policemen on each of those. I think those officers belonged to that unit but I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Just a follow-up. In addition to these two military policemen, were there officers on each of those buses as well?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see any officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Bearing in mind your previous answer about the soldiers on the buses, I assume your soldiers were not on those buses?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that if your soldiers weren't on those buses, the buses could only have been escorted by the 2nd Battalion of the military police, or was there another unit that would have been fit to carry out such tasks, apart from the two military police battalions that were part of Operations Group South?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were two military police battalions specifically, and they were trained to perform that sort of task.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Therefore, the conclusion might be either a convoy was escorted by the 1st Military Police Battalion or the 2nd. There was no other option, was there?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the 1st Battalion. Those soldiers were not under my command, then it must have been the 2nd.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you know if Major Vukasinovic had a role to play in the evacuation?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They told me that Major Vukasinovic was in barracks. He led away a group and returned them to the hospital. I did not see him myself there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did you hear at any of the briefings that he had anything to do with the hospital?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: When Major Vukasinovic came to barracks, did he not have to address the barracks security first?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily. But it was the done thing for him, as soon as he arrived, to tell him that he was there and to ask what needed doing. I'm not sure if he did or not though.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Could he possibly have got on to one of those buses there without previously requesting approval from Captain Predojevic who was guarding those buses?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He could have. He was an authorised officer from a superior command, but no one else could possibly have got on to those buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Would Captain Predojevic not have had to inform the barracks commander, Major Lukic, about Major Vukasinovic getting on to those buses?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Was Captain Predojevic not under the command of Major Lukic, as barracks commander, the commander of the 2nd Assault Detachment to which his own unit had been attached?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But the buses had arrived in the security zone of the 2nd Company. These buses were just passing through. It was some sort of a meeting point. Therefore, he had nothing to do with the persons who were on the buses, apart from securing them, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did you know that Major Lukic was there when the buses arrived, and he, of all people, was the one who ordered Captain Predojevic to secure those buses?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that specifically. Captain Predojevic called me when he had that problem. I went there to see what it was about. As soon as I realised what was going on, I informed the brigade commander and I received a specific order. I saw Lukic there at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Susic, was not Lukic the only person with the power to give an order to Captain Predojevic about securing the barracks or any persons inside the barracks, since he was both the barracks commander and the commander of the unit to which Captain Predojevic had been temporarily resubordinated, as well as the entire 2nd APC Company? Would that not seem to be a factor, sir?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. But since that company had previously been part of the 1st Battalion, and the company commander addressed me, and when I realised what this was about, I looked for a solution. So I spoke to the commander to receive an order and to see what I was supposed to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Let me just ask you something, now that we've got this far. Before you addressed the commander, had you seen at the barracks the then Lieutenant-Colonel Miodrag Panic, Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not then, but I did see him later.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: We'll get to that. Thank you. Your office, sir, at the command inside the barracks, where was it located in relation to the barracks commander Major Lukic's office?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Major Lukic was on one of the upper floors, and my office was located on the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Where was it that you called the Negoslavci command from?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From an all-terrain vehicle containing communications equipment. This was parked outside the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Does this mean that you used radio to communicate at that time?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: You used radio link, and who did you reach in Negoslavci? Who did you reach via the radio?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke to the person serving the link, and I asked to speak to the commander personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you remember who was the person serving the radio communication system at that time, and what time of the day it was?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember who the operator -- radio operator was, but it was between 10.00 and 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, on that day before 10.00 or 11.00, what did you do in the barracks? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The usual morning activities; reports from commanders, receiving those reports, giving out instructions, and preparations for further activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did you tour units within the 1st Battalion of military police?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but not prior to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: When did you tour the units? Was it after 11.00, did I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, after 2.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether that morning, on the 20th of November, there was a group of officers in the barracks from the security administration of the 1st Military District?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether that morning, in the barracks, there was a member of the command of the 1st Military District, General Gvero or General Crmaric or Colonel Ivan Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only person I know is Gvero, but I don't remember on which day I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Susic, please tell me, who was in charge of the security at the barracks? Who was in command of the security on that day, the 20th of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Captain Predojevic was responsible for the security, and the security was subordinated to Major Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you know who made it possible for this group of civilians and TO members to enter the barracks compound? Who allowed them in?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody allowed them in, that's for sure. But since there was no fence, it had been broken down, they managed to get in.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: You said that they managed to get in. Wasn't there a checkpoint or a reception desk in the barracks where they were checking people going in and out?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a reception desk. But as I told you, there was no fence around the barracks, so there was several locations where they could get in. And it was difficult to prevent them from coming in, given the regular forces that were in the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you know at all whether the barracks had security in the form of guard posts and patrols? That's how it should have been done in accordance with the regulations; it was wartime, after all.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm quite familiar with the security of the barracks because Predojevic and I organised that security. We had observation posts, we had guards, we had patrols; but it was difficult to ensure security in that large of a compound, given the regular forces that we had in the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Were you present in the barracks compound when the buses arrived from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not in the compound, and I wasn't present on the spot; nor did I know what was going on until I received a call from Captain Predojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Major Vukasinovic brought buses to the barracks; and that upon their arrival, he ordered Captain Predojevic to provide security for the buses and not allow anybody in or out? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already told you that I was told that Major Vukasinovic was there, but I didn't see him. And I don't know what he ordered to Captain Predojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Chief of Staff, Lieutenant-Colonel Miodrag Panic, also ordered Predojevic to protect the buses. And he did so when only one bus was present in the compound? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Given everything that I have put to you so far, I believe that there was no need for Captain Predojevic to address you on that occasion, because he had received his orders and instructions from Major Lukic, as the commander of the barracks, and his own superior, and from Major Vukasinovic and from Chief of Staff Panic. So there was absolutely no need for him to approach you because, at that point in time, you were not superior officer to the 2nd Company of the 1st Military Police Battalion; am I right?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it is the case, indeed, as you presented it, then you are quite right. However, when I arrived, it was necessary to undertake certain measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Susic. But in the barracks, it is the barracks commander, Major Lukic, who issued instructions and that was outside of your scope of authority. And Mr. Lukic had already done that; he was already present in the barracks at that time, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware whether he was present in the barracks at that point in time because Predojevic approached me, addressed me. And in addition to that, I knew that it was necessary to provide security, but I was wondering whether anything else, in addition to security, needed to be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: As for this, whether anything else needed to be done in addition to providing security, did you discuss it on that day in the barracks with the Chief of Staff, Miodrag Panic?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because I saw him only afterwards, after the encounter with the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did you tell him then that you had approached the commander saying that it was necessary to provide security to the people and that there would be a cabinet session held and that it would be held? And did you inform Miodrag Panic of all of these matters?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Is it your evidence, Mr. Susic, that Captain Predojevic did not tell you that he had received orders from Major Lukic, Lieutenant-Colonel Panic, Major Vukasinovic, and that he only informed you that he had problems in relation with the security?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Bulatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if Mr. Vasic intends to put such claims before the witness, then I think we need to know what was the statement given by Mr. Predojevic, who, as we know, is deceased now. And it was just put to the witness that Predojevic received orders from Lukic, from Vukasinovic, and so on. And as far as I know, there was no way that Mr. Predojevic could have informed Mr. Vasicic of all of these issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What is being put, Mr. Bulatovic, was to confirm what the evidence of the witness was, and it's put: Do you confirm that it is your evidence, in essence, that these things happened? It's not suggesting that it is the evidence of Mr. Vasic's client or witnesses or anybody else. He's merely confirming what is the position of this witness. So please continue, Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did you, at any point in time, inform Major Lukic, commander of the barracks, about the problem that arose in the compound?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Was it your duty to inform him of that, and was it Mr. Lukic who should have called the command in Negoslavci, if necessary?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether Lukic should have called, but this issue had to be resolved for the sake of security of people on the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Susic, I have to put to you the position of my client, that on that day, on the 20th of November, 1991, between 10.00 and 11.00, Colonel Mrksic did not speak to you, nor did he say anything to you either about the security or about the cabinet session. What would you say?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I disagree with such a suggestion. It is certain that I called them at that period of time, and it is certain that I received that information. I wrote that in my work notebook, which I returned to the command of the Guards Brigade after it was all filled up.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Susic, if I were to tell you that there was no need for the commander to tell you anything of the sort, because at that point in time, Chief of Staff, Miodrag Panic, was present in the barracks, would you agree with me on this?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not agree with you on this, because Commander Mrksic always issued very clear and specific orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Susic, tell me, please, how long did you have in your possession this work notebook that you just mentioned, until what year?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I returned it in late 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that in 2001, you gave a statement to the security organ of the Guards Motorised Brigade in relation to the events in Vukovar on the 20th of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember giving such a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that in that statement, you never mentioned your conversation with Mrksic, nor did you mention him saying anything to you or mentioning the cabinet session or any decisions taken there? What would you say to this suggestion of mine?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which statement of mine you have; however, if they put such a question to me then, yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: It seemed to me that you are familiar with this statement. But as it doesn't seem to be the case, I will ask the usher to give you the statement. Would you agree with me that you did not mention it?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not an authentic statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: What do you mean it's not authentic? Very well. Would you please answer my question: Is it your position that it's not authentic?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because it seems to me that this sentence was pulled out of context.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Susic. I will now suggest to you that at that time, Colonel Mrksic could not have told you that a cabinet session was in progress at that time, whether it was supposed to be decided where the people from the buses would go because, first of all, you didn't speak to him at that time. Furthermore, between 10.00 and 11.00, at which time you, according to you, spoke to him. There was no cabinet session in progress, nor was anything known about it, nor were the government or cabinet members present in Vukovar at that time. Would you accept this suggestion? For Your Honours, and my learned friends, exhibits 387, 388, and 389 are documents supporting our position.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when the cabinet session was held, I don't know where it was held, I don't know who attended it. All I know is that I had such a conversation with Colonel Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us move on to another topic. You said that from Captain Maric you heard that Commander Mrksic told him on the 18th of November to go to Ovcara. Do you know how it was that Captain Maric spoke to Mrksic, and how did he receive this order? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He only could have spoken through communication channels.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: That's an assumption. You don't actually know. He didn't tell you?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me that he called -- or rather, that Commander Mrksic called and that he ordered him to go with a squad of officers to Ovcara.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: How could Mrksic find Maric through radio communications? Can you explain that to us a bit? How?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He could have through radio communications. He knew what the channel was, and he could have reached that company at any point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: I am putting it to you that the commander of the brigade and Colonel Mrksic did not have direct communications. He could only have communicated through the superior command; and, as for the anti-terrorist company, they could only reach them either through you, while you were the commander of that company while it was still within the 1st Battalion or through the command of the 2nd Assault Detachment, when that company was within that composition; am I right?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right. That is the way things were done all the time, but this was also a possibility to reach the company that way, directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where Captain Maric was when he received this assignment?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he received that assignment, he was in his own area. That was the area of the fair grounds, Sajmiste.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did he tell you what forces he took along to carry out this assignment, and what he was planning to do if he did, indeed, call you the way you said he did?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He took one squad of officers with three Puch vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: I assume that he took the commander of that squad, would that be logical?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, most probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Mr. Susic, why did Captain Maric call you when he was no longer under your command at that point in time? Do you have an explanation for that?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maric was within the 1st Battalion then, because that was on the 18th when the company was within the 1st Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: It seemed to me that at the beginning of my questioning, you said that he was within the 2nd Assault Detachment?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: From the 4th until the 20th of November?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 20th of October [as interpreted] up until the 20th of October. The anti-terrorist company was within the 2nd Assault Detachment from the 2nd of October until the 20th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you know -- or rather, where were you when he called you and said that?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must have been on my way to the briefing, because it was around 1800 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what task Captain Maric's unit was carrying out then, and at what particular facility, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, it was engaged in combat activities. Part of the unit was in the high school, Gimnazija, and the others were at the command post, Sajmiste, the stadium, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: I have to say that Colonel Mrksic never issued any orders to Captain Maric via radio communications; he never used that. He used regular channels for issuing orders through unit commanders, which is the only logical way to do it; right?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is logical as well. A commander can issue an order that way, especially as it is the anti-terrorist company that is involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us go back to barracks for a moment. You mentioned that you saw there an unknown colonel and a captain from the Territorial Defence, am I right?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: May I just interrupt one moment with the utmost respect. I'm afraid, perhaps it's my fault, but I don't understand the sequence of questions starting at 23:15 through to 23:25, because it seems to be contradictory. Is my learned friend saying that Maric did or did not receive an order from Mrksic in any event, or is the issue that he did receive an order but it was by a particular method through which this officer would have had control or would have had knowledge? Because as the way the matters stand now, in my submission, it is not clear the way the case is being put, and it seems to be almost contradictory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic, can you clarify the position?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course I can. Mr. Mrksic did not issue an order to Captain Maric in any way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And while you're interrupted on the matter, you did put to the witness, transcript page 20, lines 19 to 20, a statement of his from 1992. You mentioned documents 387, 388 and 389, but which one of those was it that you put to the witness? The transcript isn't clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall clarify both matters, Your Honour. Thank you. I did not put any one of these exhibits to the witness. I just said that these were the relevant exhibits. These were the ones that we introduced according to 92 bis, at the request of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... show the witness then.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I showed the witness his statement that he gave to the security organs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not an exhibit, Your Honour. He said that it's not authentic, so I thought that I wouldn't use it further on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. As long as it's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: We came to the commander of the Territorial Defence. Let's put it this way: Do you remember what they wore?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: SMB uniforms, olive-green/grey. The uniform of ours that was there before the camouflage uniform. They were pretty far away from me and I was almost in front of the barracks, in front of the building itself. Predojevic was going with them. They toured the buses and set out with one vehicle in front of the buses and another vehicle behind the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Susic, did you ask them to show you their IDs?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did you ask them what they were doing there, what their intention was?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I did not even meet with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Was the barracks commander there, Major Lukic?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: He was not with those persons there within the compound?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: You didn't ask Captain Predojevic why he was talking to these persons, and what they wanted?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't ask him. They passed by, they left on the buses, and they left the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: I have to put it to you that you did not do all of that, because you were not in charge of all of that. Major Lukic, as commander of the barracks, was in charge of that?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course he was, but I saw the buses leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: You were there when the buses left. Tell me, who escorted these buses?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the buses, there were the same policemen who had been there at the front door and at the back door, and the same drivers, except that there were two all-terrain vehicles; one in front, and one in the back. And they set out in the direction of Negoslavci.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did you find out what unit escorted these buses, at least later at briefings?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: On the 20th, as for the arrival of -- in barracks and then going to Ovcara and then the government meeting and the events in Ovcara, were they a topic at the briefing, and were you present at the briefing at all on the 20th of November?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was present, but I do not recall the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: What about the 21st of November? Do you remember whether you attended the briefing then, and whether the events from Ovcara from the previous night were on the agenda of that briefing?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There weren't any specificities.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether you were in barracks on the 21st of November?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did you see Panic, Lukic, and Sljivancanin then in the barracks, and do you remember anything particular can concerning the 21st?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, some journalists were there. I remember that, but I wasn't really dealing with that matter at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: When was it that you first heard that at Ovcara, a temporary camp for prisoners of war was established?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not even hear of it having been established and I don't even know where it was, and I never was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: My last question pertains - I mean from this part - pertains to this colonel you referred to in barracks. Did you ever ask anyone who this colonel was who was in barracks? Did you ever ask Major Lukic, Miodrag Panic anything about that? Did you ever learn about who that colonel was?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not learn anything about that colonel. I just know that he was not from the Guards Brigade. Because had he been from the Guards Brigade, I would have known him.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Susic, for your answers. Your Honours, I have no further questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vasic. Could I just correct one thing I said when speaking to you about that statement. It was a statement given in 2001, not in 1992, just so the record is clear. Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon. We heard here that Milovo Brdo fell on the 10th of November, do you know that, too?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know, but I won't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Do you know from the fall of Milovo Brdo until the liberation of Vukovar, on what axis of activity was the 2nd Assault Detachment?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 2nd Assault Detachment, I don't know. I think that it still had the same axis throughout this period.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we briefly move into private session, Your Honours, please, very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether the chief of general staff, General Adzic, ever visited Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Fair enough, thank you. Do you know Captain Miroslav Radic?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: On the 20th of November, 1991, we're talking about what went on in the barracks. On that particular day, did you see him within the barracks at any point in time?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see him in the barracks on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And you didn't hear of him being there?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't even hear of him being there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You say that Major Vukasinovic led a group of people off the bus and sent them to the hospital, you say that. My question is: This group consisting of between 15 and 20 people, they arrived on the bus in the barracks, and were from there returned from the hospital; is that the group you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the second part. And it's leading, in any event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The whole conversation is about what the witness was told by somebody, if I remember, he doesn't say that he knew any of these things personally. I can see your point, Mr. Moore, but I'm reading the whole thing in the context of this witness is only speaking about what he's being told.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: It's the phrase that "you say," as if he has personal knowledge of fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Perhaps confusing. Mr. Borovic, I believe I'm correct in my recollection that the witness doesn't suggest he saw or that he knows, merely he's been told. If your questions -- if you're content with that and your questions proceed on that basis, go ahead; otherwise, correct it somehow.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's my interpretation, too. I said the witness says that he heard. I think that was fair. Just for Mr. Moore's benefit, I think Vukasinovic will be coming along, and he'll be telling us what it was exactly that he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You said that at the head of that column of buses leaving the barracks was a Puch military vehicle; and in that vehicle, were the colonel and the Territorial Defence captain?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's an all-terrain vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: The captain and the colonel were inside that vehicle; right?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you see Captain Miroslav Radic in that Puch, which was at the head of the column?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What if I tell you that we had an OTP witness here who stated that Captain Miroslav Radic was this that vehicle at the head of the bus column.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Sorry. I object to that question, again, because the witness said that he didn't see Captain Radic. He's being asked to give opinion evidence in relation to what a witness said earlier on. The answer has been given, and my learned friend is merely repeating it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like Mr. Moore to respect the established procedure in the courtroom. Wait for the answer first, before an objection is raised. If that rule applies to the Defence, I suppose it should likewise apply to the OTP. At any rate, we heard the witness's answer. And this being my last answer, I would now like to put the Miroslav Radic Defence position.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: There was an OTP witness who said there was a Puch at the head of that bus convoy, and Miroslav Radic was in it. But there was no mention of the TO captain, so my question is: Is that witness's testimony true or is what you're saying true, that in that Puch, there were the TO captain and the colonel? So in other words, would you say that the witness, who said that, was lying, that Captain Radic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continued...] Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Radic was not this that Puch.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, this concludes my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Borovic, and what I said at line -- page 31, line 24 was "or mistaken." The transcript couldn't pick it up because we were both talking. Can I make clear, Mr. Borovic, for the future, that I established a rule of practice affecting interjections in questioning by other Defence counsel; because A, there was a very growing frequency of those interjections, B, many of them came at critical points of cross-examination, and C, many of them immediately suggested answers that the witness was able to pick up on. So it is a rule that applied when there was multiple Defence counsel, and it applied to Defence counsel. Thank you. Mr. Moore, we've got three or four minutes. Would you think it better to start after the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can deal with a short topic in closed session; and after that, we can have our break, if that's acceptable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well, closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Moore, I believe we now need to adjourn for the first break and we will resume at five minutes to the hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Moore.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Susic, would it be right to say that you attended briefings at OG South on a daily basis?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the 1st of November on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And would it be correct to say, just using common sense, that some of the people you would recognise because they came from the Guards Brigade, but there would be other people who were not from the Guards Brigade who were at those briefings; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, but for the most part, at briefings, there would be the commander, the assistant commanders and the battalion commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: But you also had liaison officers who were attached to OG South.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, there was Colonel Pavkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Now, can I just deal with one or two other matters. I want to focus, if I may, on the briefing of the 19th, the 6.00 p.m. briefing, or the 1800 hours as the military like to call it. So can we just focus on that topic, please. At that time, Vukovar had fallen and evacuation procedures had commenced; that is correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: It is also correct to say that one of the main tasks of the military police was the assistance of evacuations of persons; that is also correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: In relation to those evacuations, at that time, we have seen from the orders of OG South and elsewhere that there was an expected evacuation of the Vukovar Hospital. You were aware of that as well, in general terms; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I wasn't aware of how the hospital would be evacuated, would the ICRC be in charge, or whoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You may not have been aware of the actual nuts and bolts, but you were aware that in principle, the hospital had to be evacuated by someone; that is correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the hospital was not within the area held by the battalion; therefore, I wasn't specifically aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I am not specifically -- or I'm not referring to the specifics; I'm referring to the generalities. Because while the hospital had originally been in the zone of responsibility of OG North, OG South had responsibility for it from approximately the 18th of November. You were aware of that fact, weren't you, in general terms?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was aware of that, and I was also aware of the fact that the 2nd Battalion was securing the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I don't want to talk about securing hospital. I just want to deal with the generality of the evacuation of the hospital; do you follow?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, but I don't know how it was evacuated.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So as of the 18th, and probably I'd suggest before, you were aware, in general terms, that the hospital had to be evacuated by someone; that is correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware of the need for evacuation, but I didn't know whether the ICRC would be in charge of that or perhaps someone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: However, the time came when you went to a briefing on the 19th of November, and you were aware, in general terms, that the hospital had not been evacuated by the time of that briefing; that is correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of that. I was not aware of anything about the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So you had made no inquiry, and there had been no general discussion about the possibility of evacuation of the hospital with you; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. I made no inquiry, nor did anyone put me in charge of anything at all to do with the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: But as I said, I want to deal with the generality. We'll deal with your tasks in a moment. Would it be right to say that there was a possibility of you and your unit being involved in the evacuation? I'm not saying you were; I am merely asking whether there was a possibility that that would have occurred?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we could have been involved, as a possibility, but our battalion was quite stretched out. So that's one thing that you had to keep in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I am merely dealing with the possibility, the possibility that existed when you went to the briefing at 1800 hours on the 19th of November; that is correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, anything was possible. The simple truth is, I didn't receive such assignment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: The point I'm that I am attempting to make is quite simply this: You were in charge of a military police battalion with the possibility of being involved in the evacuation of the possibility; and, therefore, I would suggest, if there had been mention of the evacuation on the 19th briefing, that would have been something that you would have been listening either for or to; do you agree?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do agree, but I heard nothing about that; therefore, I had no knowledge about that particular task.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So are you saying - because your reply seemed to be equivocal when you were being cross-examined by Mr. Mrksic's counsel - are you saying there was no mention of an evacuation by Mrksic on the 19th; is that what you are saying? Because if there had, you would have remembered.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he mentioned that or not. What I do know is that I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, you would have remembered on the 20th when five buses with individuals arrived on your doorstep, wouldn't you, if they were unannounced?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it had been mentioned, I probably would have remembered. But, no, I didn't know this. This came as quite a surprise.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So the mental state that you had, as far as you can recollect, is the 19th, you do not recollect if there was mention of an evacuation by Mrksic. On the 20th when the buses arrived, it came - and I use the English phrase - "as a bolt from the blue." It came completely unexpected; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Dealing with reality, on the 20th of November, knowing what had occurred, what did you think these people were, or who they were when they arrived?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I wasn't there when the buses arrived. I arrived when Captain Predojevic called me. When I reached the buses on which there were civilians, there were about 50 locals around the buses wearing civilian clothes and uniforms, and some were armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Never mind whether Captain Predojevic mentioned anything to you. I want to know what your thought processes were when you were informed that five buses had come through loaded with people. So, what did you think? What did you know? Tell us.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What did I think? First of all, I went there to see what was going on; that was the first thing that sprang to mind, so I went.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, did you ask: Who on earth are these people? Because I have never been told about such a group of people coming into my area?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I asked the driver, who was in the front of one of the buses, and he said: "From the hospital." And Predojevic had previously told me the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can I suggest that the first question you would have asked is: Who is in charge of this? Who do I speak to? Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. But I do not see a single officer there, so I decided to speak to the driver to see where these people were from.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So you asked the driver: Who is in charge of this? That is correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I asked him where these people were from; and he said they came from the hospital, were to be collected there, and sent on to Sremska Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So that was the bus driver's understanding at that time. They were to be held there and then they were going to Sremska Mitrovica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: But I return to the point that I -- or the question I pose, and it is this: You're an officer. You've got five buses with individuals -- and we'll come to that in a moment. It is a logical, indeed proper question to ask: Who is in charge? Who, as an officer, do I speak to? Now, I suggest to you that you must have asked that question.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no officers there at the time with the buses. There were drivers and military policemen; one each at the front and back doors. The buses were closed, and there was no one for me to ask in the area with the exception of Captain Predojevic who told me the same thing that the driver had told me previously, that those people had arrived from the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: We talk about a group of people; it's a group of men; that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So this is not a random group; this is a selected group, just on probability theory. That is also correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. There were men on though buses, and I have no idea who put them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And it's the much more than just men, a selected group on the buses; there were two soldiers armed at either end of the bus. That is right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two per bus; one at the front or one at the rear door. The doors were shut and no one was leaving, and they were sitting on the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: But the question is, and the question I'd suggest that you must have asked: Who or what are they? Because it is essential to know who or what are they to assess the possibility of attack and ensuring proper security; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Those were people from the hospital, that's what I was told. Now I knew that those were people from the hospital. The locals around them were calling out their names, individually, accusing them of having wronged them in some way, burned down their house, killed one of their relatives or expelled some of their relatives. And there was a degree of commotion around the scene. I realised that the situation was gaining in complexity.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Is the phrase "gaining in complexity" the same as "getting out of control"?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not getting out of control, but with the distinct possibility of getting out of control.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean "the distinct possibility of getting out of control?"

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you have an unhappy crowd and if some people are actually armed, somebody can always start shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And so, therefore, shooting was a possibility; that is correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, whenever there are weapons around, it can always come to a shoot-out.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, it's hardly going to come to a shoot-out with about 250 people in a bus, who are unarmed, and a group of TOs, who might be armed outside. I would suggest that you had an extremely vulnerable group of people in those buses; that is correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps, but that's why I was there, to take measures to prevent anything like that from happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: We have heard evidence. I'm not going to go through tranches of it. But did you ever see, for example - it's at page 5285 - reference to people showing knives and making gestures indicating that "he would slit my throat and cut off my head?" You didn't see any people with knives making those sort of gestures, by any chance?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a degree of verbal harassment. But there were soldiers standing between the crowd and the buses, so I didn't really delve into those details that much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: It's not a question of delving into details. It's a question of having a pair of ears and hearing what was going on and a pair of eyes and seeing what was going on, isn't it, in reality?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In reality, precisely. I realised the situation was complex, and I said what to do. I knew that we needed to secure that, but how long would they be staying there for? Was there anything else I should do about the buses or the men there, in addition to securing them. And that's why I requested additional orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And again, just one other little tranche, 3643, P012. "Q. These local Serbs, were they armed or in any sort of uniform? "A. They were armed. They had knives that they threatened us with. They went from bus to bus, threatening to slaughter us, kill us, and so on. They were dressed in different clothes, some had fur hats, some had beards, some had the top part of a uniform or the bottom part, not a full JNA uniform, perhaps, just a portion of it. Those were paramilitaries, among them were some JNA soldiers, too." Now what I want to ask you this: You mentioned that people were armed. I anticipate that you may accept that. Well, people had knives. Did you see individuals with fur hats, sometimes known as Chetniks?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, exactly, there were some who wore civilian clothes. There were some who had mixed attire, bottom civilian, top uniform, different variations thereof. They wore different clothes. They had different head gear, hats, whatever. I could not really perceive each and every detail then, because I was supposed to do something different, how to make sure that no incident occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can I take it that the description that I have just read out, you would consider that to be a fair assessment or reflection of what you saw?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sort of. Almost.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And as a direct consequence of what you saw, you then say you went and spoke to Mrksic. I want to deal with an area of evidence before we get there. Mr. Vasic was asking questions of you: Why on earth you were involved because in actual fact, on the normal chain of command, it should have been Lukic. So I repeat that question: Why is it you were involved?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Predojevic was, before entering the 2nd Assault Detachment, within the 1st Battalion. Until I became the commander on the 1st of November, I was within the 2nd Assault Detachment, and I was responsible there. Predojevic addressed me. Now, I don't know whether at that moment, Major Lukic was there. And I went to the spot and set out to resolve that, so I could resolve that, or rather, through the company commander who was commanding. I did not interfere in his command; I just helped him resolve that task.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Would it be right to say that you were surprised to receive a telephone call from Predojevic because, in reality, you would have expected him to contact Lukic first?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether Lukic was there, Major Lukic, whether he was there on the spot, and that was supposed to be resolved as soon as possible. It's better to resolve it in the beginning, rather than later when it's too late.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I would suggest to you, you have not answered the question. It is right, isn't it, that on the proper chain of command, or line of command, Lukic should have been contacted, not you. Whether he was there or not is another issue, but that is the person who should have been contacted; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is certainly right. Now, did he look for him and not find him, and perhaps he could not have waited any longer. He didn't have enough time and then he addressed me. At any rate, I went to resolve that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I do not criticise in any way, please understand. But can I suggest to you the reason that Predojevic contacted you was because the situation was getting out of control, and he was extremely concerned about approximate? That is right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The situation was not getting out of control, but it could have gotten out of control if it were to continue that way. Perhaps it could, perhaps it couldn't. But perhaps his assessment was that it could get out of control, and it's better that he dealt with it that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Bulatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, for the sake of fairness, I would ask the Prosecutor not to speculate, not to ask the witness to say what another witness thought when he addressed him. How can this witness know what another person was thinking at the moment when he asked him something? Or things along those lines. I'm saying that for the sake of the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Moore.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What did Predojevic say to you that caused you to go to see what was happening?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said to me that in barracks, there are buses on which there are civilians, and that around the buses are locals who are threatening the civilians who are on the buses, and that there could be a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And did he then ask you to come down, or did you go voluntarily or, should I say, of your own volition?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He asked me to come because he was seeking a solution. In order to find a solution, I went to see what there was all about so I would see for myself what was going on at the actual spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did he say whether he had seen the buses arrive?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't ask him how the buses arrived. He confirmed to me that these were buses that had come from the hospital and that they were supposed to stay there temporarily.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So how long did you remain with the buses before returning to make a telephone call or communication with Mrksic?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not more than ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Through that period, did you see any other officer there?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That period, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: If we follow the sequence, it's right you then returned to the barracks; is that right? To your office, presumably, to make contact with Mrksic; would I be right in that?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. Not to the office. I had a vehicle in front of the building where there were communications devices, so I went to that vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Are you saying, then, that you made contact from a vehicle as opposed to a building? So you returned to the vehicle as opposed to your office?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. From there, I could have complete communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
